unit.title: Coordinate the installation of electrical equipment, ancillary apparatus and secondary wiring

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Before a new switchboard is ordered for a factory, what should the coordinator check against the specification?
options: Only the price, as long as it fits through the door
Its ratings, fault rating, IP rating, size and access
Only the colour of the paint used on the enclosure doors
Which maker the last contractor happened to use

questions.stem: A control panel is delivered to site. What should be checked before it is signed for?
options: Damage, and that the nameplate matches the order
Only that the delivery driver has a valid licence
That the panel is already wired to the motors
That the doors are locked and the keys are inside

questions.stem: A switchboard arrives two weeks before its room is ready. How should it be stored?
options: Outdoors on the bare ground, under a tree for some shade
In the open, with its doors left open for air
Upright, covered, dry and secure, as the maker says
On its back in the car park, to save some space

questions.stem: A 900 kg transformer must be moved into a plant room. What should come first?
options: Ask the strongest workers on site to carry it in together
Roll it in on short lengths of steel conduit
Lift it by its terminal bushings with a rope
A lift plan using its lifting points and trained people

questions.stem: Why must the centre of gravity be known before lifting a tall control cabinet?
options: To work out how much the cabinet cost
To decide which colour of sling to use
So the load does not tip or swing when lifted
So that the doors stay closed while it moves

questions.stem: A standby generator needs a concrete plinth. With whom should the electrical coordinator agree its size and holding-down bolts?
options: The painting contractor on the job
The client's office cleaner
The supplier's delivery driver
The civil or building contractor

questions.stem: Why must a floor-standing switchboard be levelled and anchored before cables are connected?
options: So it is the same height as the doors around it
So doors and parts line up and it cannot topple
So the cables can be pulled in more tightly
So that it can easily be moved again later

questions.stem: Shelving is planned right in front of a new distribution board in a storeroom. What should the coordinator do?
options: Have the shelving moved so the access space stays clear
Allow it, as the shelves can be emptied when needed
Fit the board behind the shelves so it is protected
Ask the client to keep only light boxes on those shelves

questions.stem: A variable speed drive is to be fitted in a small closed cupboard. What should be checked?
options: That the cupboard is painted a light colour
That the drive is mounted upside down to save space
That the cupboard door has a lock and a key
That heat can escape, as the maker's data requires

questions.stem: Which drawing shows where each part is mounted inside a control panel?
options: The single-line diagram for the site
The panel layout (general arrangement) drawing
The schematic of the control circuit
The floor plan of the building

questions.stem: What is the main use of a terminal (connection) diagram?
options: It shows which wire lands on which terminal
It shows how the control circuit works, in order
It shows the size and the weight of the panel
It shows the route of the cables outside

questions.stem: Why does each control wire in a panel carry a numbered marker at each end?
options: So the wiring looks expensive and well made
So each wire can be charged to the client
So each wire can be traced on the drawings
So all the wires can be cut to one length

questions.stem: Why are ferrules crimped onto fine stranded control wires before they go into screw terminals?
options: So all the strands are held firmly in the terminal
So the wire can carry a much higher current
So the bare end is fully insulated in the terminal
So the colour of the wire can be seen more clearly

questions.stem: What is DIN rail used for in a control panel?
options: Carrying the panel's main incoming cable
Earthing the panel door to the enclosure
Mounting contactors, relays and terminals
Holding the panel's drawings and papers

questions.stem: Why is the slotted wiring duct in a panel not packed completely full?
options: So that it weighs less when the panel is lifted
So that the cover can be left off for a neat look
So that the colours of the wires can be seen
To let heat out and leave room for changes

questions.stem: Where should the signal cable from a tank level sensor be run inside a panel?
options: Tied tightly together with the motor's power cables
Away from power wiring, screened as the design says
Through the same gland as the 220 V supply cable
Loose across the busbars to keep the run short

questions.stem: Why are contactor and breaker terminals tightened to the maker's torque figure?
options: To make the job take longer and look more careful
Loose ones overheat; over-tight ones get damaged
So that the screws can never be undone again
To raise the voltage rating of each terminal

questions.stem: A current transformer's (CT's) secondary wires have been left disconnected, and the cable through it is about to carry load. What is the danger?
options: A dangerously high voltage can appear across it
The CT will then read the current twice as high
The meter connected to it will run backwards
The primary cable will lose all of its current

questions.stem: During installation, the meter for a CT circuit has not yet arrived. What should be fitted at the CT's test terminals, so it is safe when the supply is later switched on?
options: A fuse in series with the CT's secondary
A larger meter with a higher current range
A shorting link across the secondary terminals
A label saying that the meter is missing

questions.stem: Why is a large machine's control circuit often fed at a low voltage, such as 24 V, from a control transformer?
options: So that the contactors switch the motor faster
So that the main fuses can be left out
So that the motor uses less power at full load
To lower the shock risk at buttons and sensors

questions.stem: A forward-reverse starter has two contactors. Why are they interlocked?
options: So both can close together for more power
So the motor runs faster when in reverse
So both can never close at once and short the supply
So that no overload relay is needed on the starter any more

questions.stem: Why is a correctly sized cable gland used where a cable enters an outdoor panel?
options: So the cable can be pulled out easily later
So that the gland matches the panel's colour
So the panel can be lifted by its cables
To grip the cable and keep the IP rating

questions.stem: After installation, a panel has an unused knockout hole open in its side. What should be done?
options: Leave it open so that the panel can breathe
Close it with a proper blanking plug
Cover it with tape from the inside
Use it to pass a hose in for cleaning

questions.stem: Why might the specification ask for surge protection at the main board of a building on a hilltop in Jamaica?
options: Lightning and switching surges can damage equipment
To make the lights in the building shine brighter
To lower the building's monthly electricity bill
To stop the RCDs from tripping on real faults

questions.stem: Before a PLC-controlled panel is powered for the first time, how is its input wiring checked?
options: By switching on and pressing every button quickly
By asking the PLC programmer to check it later on
By measuring the voltage at each input with the power on
Point to point with a continuity tester and the drawings

questions.stem: When a new control panel is first energised by a competent person, why is the control circuit often powered alone first, with the motor supply still isolated?
options: So that the motor can be started much more quickly later
To prove the controls and interlocks before motors run
Because the control circuit uses more power
So the client can calibrate the meters first

questions.stem: How should a panel's hinged metal door that carries push-buttons be earthed?
options: With a flexible earth strap to the enclosure
Through its hinges only, since they are metal
By painting it with a conductive paint
It needs no earth if its buttons are plastic

questions.stem: A UPS with vented lead-acid batteries is to be installed in a small room. What must the coordinator make sure of?
options: The room is sealed tight so that no dust gets in
The batteries stand directly on a damp floor
The room is ventilated, as the maker requires
The batteries are stacked on top of the UPS

questions.stem: The voltage on a new three-phase compressor's nameplate does not match the site supply. What should the coordinator do?
options: Hold it, and refer it to the designer and supplier
Connect it anyway, since motors adjust to any supply
Fit it, then wait to see whether it overheats
Change the supply voltage at the main board

questions.stem: After terminals are torqued, why do some installers mark each screw with a paint line?
options: To show which of the wires is the earth
To make the panel look properly finished
To show it was torqued and reveal any movement
To stop the screw from rusting in damp air

questions.stem: Why does a specification often ask for spare terminals and space in a new control panel?
options: So the panel weighs the same as the drawing
So the supplier can sell a bigger enclosure
So the installer can leave out some parts
So changes can be added without a new panel

questions.stem: What should the label on a new item of switchgear show?
options: The installer's home address
What it controls and where it is fed from
The price that was paid for it
The date the building was designed

questions.stem: A trainee has wired a panel from the schematic. What is the best way for the coordinator to check it before power-up?
options: Look quickly at the front of the panel
A wire-by-wire check against the drawings
Ask the trainee whether he is sure it is right
Switch it on and see whether anything trips

questions.stem: During wiring, the crew must add a relay that is not on the drawing. What should happen to the drawings?
options: Mark up the change and get it approved
Leave them, since the panel is what matters
Throw away the old set of drawings
Write the change on the door in marker pen

questions.stem: A large switchboard will not fit through the plant room's finished doorway. How could this have been avoided?
options: By buying a smaller board with fewer circuits
By taking the board apart on site without asking
By checking the access route and timing early
By asking the builder to knock out the wall later

questions.stem: What is recorded on a commissioning sheet for a motor control panel?
options: The names of the crew's family members
The weather on the day the panel arrived
The price of each part fitted in the panel
Settings, test results and who witnessed them

questions.stem: To protect it, a pump must not restart until 3 minutes after it stops. Which device is set to do this?
options: A float switch
A photocell
A time-delay relay (timer)
A surge protector

questions.stem: A pressure transmitter sends a 4–20 mA signal. Why is it useful that its zero is 4 mA and not 0 mA?
options: It lets the loop work with no supply at all
It makes the signal immune to all electrical noise
It doubles the measuring range of the transmitter
A broken wire reads 0 mA, so it can be spotted

questions.stem: A control panel will be mounted outdoors near the sea in St Thomas. Which enclosure is the best choice?
options: An indoor-grade painted mild steel enclosure
Stainless steel or plastic, with a suitable IP rating
An open frame, so that the sea breeze can blow through it
Any enclosure, as long as it is repainted yearly

questions.stem: Several electricians will connect equipment to one isolated switchboard. How should it be locked off?
options: A group hasp, with each person's own padlock
One padlock, with its key hung on the board
The supervisor holds the breaker off by hand
A note on the board saying not to switch on

questions.stem: Why must a power factor correction capacitor bank be left to discharge before its terminals are touched?
options: It needs time to cool down after it has been switched off
Its fuses must reset themselves before it is safe
Its meter must first return to a zero reading
Capacitors can hold a dangerous charge after isolation

questions.stem: Why is the client's representative invited to witness the commissioning tests?
options: So they can do the tests instead of the electricians
So they see the equipment work and can accept it
So the electricians are able to leave site early
So the client can choose the colour of the panel

questions.stem: A chiller's control panel needs signals from the building management system. With whom must the electrical coordinator agree the list of signals?
options: The mechanical contractor and the controls specialist
Only the newest trainee working in the electrical crew
The security guard on duty at the site gate
The company that supplied the cable tray

questions.stem: At the handover of a new pump station, which documents must go to the client?
options: Only the receipts for the cable that was bought
The crew's overtime records for the whole job
Manuals, drawings, settings and test records
The coordinator's own daily diary of the job

questions.stem: A control circuit has 4 contactor coils that each need 12 VA to stay pulled in, and 6 indicator lamps of 2 VA each. What total VA must the control transformer supply with all of them on?
options: 48 VA
72 VA
60 VA
24 VA

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the drawing called that shows a whole electrical system with single lines, from the supply to the main boards?
What is the slotted plastic channel with a clip-on cover that carries the wiring inside a panel called?
What are the connectors called, clipped side by side on a rail, where field cables meet the panel wiring?
In which unit is a terminal's tightening torque usually given?
A control transformer is rated 100 VA at 24 V. About how many amps can it supply at most? (Give one decimal place.)
In control systems, what is the full name of a PLC?
What is the plan called that lists each inspection and test to be done, when it is done, and who signs for it?
What is the list called that shows every PLC input and output with its address and the device on it?
What is the order in which the three phases reach their peaks called, which sets a motor's direction?
Which gas can build up while lead-acid batteries are charging, so the room needs ventilation?
What kind of drawing shows how a control circuit works, with each line read from top to bottom?
Which fabric lifting accessory is used to lift equipment without damaging its paint?
What is the trained person called who gives signals to the crane operator during a lift?
What is the list of small defects called, found during commissioning, that must be put right before handover?
A panel has 120 wires to terminate, and a trainee terminates 15 wires an hour. How many hours will it take?

essays.stem: Describe how you would coordinate the installation of a large floor-standing switchboard in a new plant room, from approval of the equipment to connecting the cables.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check the switchboard's details against the specification: ratings, fault rating, IP rating, size, weight and cable entry. Once it is approved, I agree the delivery date with the supplier and the main contractor. I check the plant room drawings with the builder: the plinth or floor level, holding-down bolts, cable trenches or ducts, the doorway size and the route from the delivery point, so the board can get in. I make sure the room is finished, dry and lockable before delivery, or arrange safe storage. On delivery I inspect it for damage and check the nameplate. A lift plan is made for moving it into place, using the lifting points and trained people. The board is positioned with the clear working space in front, levelled, anchored and the sections bolted and bonded together. I coordinate with the air-conditioning trade for ventilation. Cables are brought in through the correct glands, and all work is done with the board isolated, locked off and proved dead. Every step is recorded.
markingPoints: Checks the equipment against the specification
Agrees delivery, plinth, trenches and access route with other trades
Room ready or safe storage; receiving inspection
Lift plan; positioned with clearances, levelled, anchored, bonded
Cable entry, safe isolation and records

essays.stem: Explain the checks you would make when receiving electrical equipment and ancillary apparatus on site, and what you would do about any problems.
essays.modelAnswer: I check each delivery against the purchase order, the approved submittal and the specification. I count the items and check the type, quantity and part numbers. I read the nameplates: voltage, frequency, current rating, number of phases, IP rating and control voltage must match what was ordered and suit Jamaica's 50 Hz supply. I look for transit damage, such as dents, broken doors, cracked insulators, loose parts or water inside, and I check the shock or tilt indicators on large items. I make sure the manuals, drawings, test certificates, keys and spare parts are included. Any problem is written on the delivery note before signing, photographed and reported to the supplier and my supervisor at once. Damaged or wrong items are labelled 'do not use' and kept apart, so nobody installs them by mistake. Good items go into dry, secure storage as the maker says. I update the materials record so the project team knows what has arrived and what is still due.
markingPoints: Checks against order, submittal and specification
Checks nameplate ratings, including 50 Hz and control voltage
Inspects for damage and checks documents and accessories are included
Records problems on the delivery note, photographs and reports them
Quarantines faulty items, stores good ones correctly, updates records

essays.stem: Describe good practice for the secondary (control) wiring inside a panel: layout, wire marking, terminations, segregation and records.
essays.modelAnswer: The layout follows the panel layout drawing: parts are mounted on DIN rail with space for heat and spare capacity, and wiring duct runs between rows. Field cables land on terminal blocks, never straight onto devices. Each wire is cut to length, run in the duct without crossing over parts, and not packed so tightly that the cover will not close. Every wire is marked at both ends with its number from the schematic, so it can be traced. Fine stranded wires have ferrules crimped on with the right tool, and every terminal is tightened to the maker's torque figure, with only as many wires per terminal as the maker allows. Control colours follow the specification. Power and control wiring are kept apart, and signal cables are screened and separated from power, with the screen earthed as the design says. The door is earthed with a flexible strap. Any change is marked on the drawings and approved, and a copy of the final drawings is left in the panel's document pocket.
markingPoints: Layout follows the drawing, with DIN rail, duct and spare space
Each wire numbered at both ends to the schematic
Correct terminations: ferrules, torque, terminal blocks for field cables
Segregation of power, control and signal wiring; door earth
Changes marked up and approved; drawings left with the panel

essays.stem: Explain how you would check a newly wired control panel before it is energised for the first time.
essays.modelAnswer: With the panel isolated, locked off, tagged and proved dead with a tester checked before and after, I first inspect it. I compare it with the layout drawing and parts list: correct parts, ratings and settings, such as overload and timer settings. I check that nothing is loose, no tools or offcuts are left inside, glands and blanking plugs are fitted, and covers are on. Then I check the wiring point to point against the schematic and terminal diagram, ticking off each wire on the drawing, and I check wire numbers. I test continuity of the protective conductors, including the door strap. I carry out insulation resistance tests on the power circuits, with electronic devices such as the PLC, drives and surge protectors disconnected or as the maker says. I check CT circuits are complete or shorted. I record all results. Only then does a competent person energise the panel, usually the control circuit first with the motor supplies isolated, to prove the controls and interlocks.
markingPoints: Safe isolation with tester checked before and after
Visual inspection against layout and parts list, including settings
Point-to-point wiring check against the drawings
Protective conductor continuity and insulation tests, protecting electronics; CT circuits checked
Records results; staged energising by a competent person

essays.stem: Explain the dangers of current transformer (CT) circuits and capacitors during installation and maintenance, and how you would make them safe.
essays.modelAnswer: A current transformer steps a large current down to a small one for a meter or relay. If its secondary is left open while current flows in the primary, a very high voltage can appear across the secondary terminals, which can give a deadly shock and destroy the CT. So the secondary must always be connected to its meter or relay, or shorted with the shorting link at the test terminals, before the primary is energised, and the link is only removed when the meter circuit is complete. Capacitors, such as power factor correction banks, motor capacitors and the capacitors inside drives and UPS units, can hold a dangerous charge after the supply is isolated. Before touching them, I isolate, lock off, tag and prove dead with a tester checked before and after, then wait the discharge time on the maker's label and check that the voltage has fallen, discharging through a proper resistor where the maker allows. I warn the crew about these hazards and put labels on the equipment.
markingPoints: Explains the high-voltage danger of an open CT secondary
CT secondary kept connected or shorted before energising
Explains stored charge in capacitors, drives and UPS units
Isolate, prove dead, wait the discharge time and check before touching
Warns the crew and labels the equipment

essays.stem: Explain how you would plan the safe lift of a heavy item of equipment, such as a 1-tonne transformer, into its final position.
essays.modelAnswer: I start with the maker's data: the weight, the lifting points and the centre of gravity. I survey the route from the delivery point to the final position, checking the ground or floor strength, doorways, slopes and overhead obstructions such as cables. I choose the method: a crane, forklift, or skates and jacks, and lifting gear such as slings and shackles rated for the load, with current inspection tags. I write a lift plan and risk assessment giving the method, the equipment, the people and the exclusion zone. Only trained and authorised people operate the crane or forklift, sling the load and give signals, and one person is in charge. On the day I check the weather, because strong wind makes a crane lift unsafe, and I brief the team. The area is barriered and nobody stands under the load. The load is lifted a little first to check balance, then moved slowly with tag lines. It is set down gently on its plinth, then levelled and anchored.
markingPoints: Uses the maker's weight, lifting points and centre of gravity
Surveys the route and floor strength
Chooses rated, inspected equipment; trained people with one in charge
Lift plan, risk assessment, briefing and exclusion zone
Test lift, controlled movement, then set down, level and anchor

essays.stem: Describe how you would supervise a team of four wiring two control panels at the same time, so that the quality stays high and the drawings stay correct.
essays.modelAnswer: I start by making sure everyone has the same, latest set of drawings, and that old drawings are removed. I explain the standard expected: wire sizes and colours, numbering, ferrules, torque and tidy duct work, and I show a sample. I split the work, for example two people per panel, with the more experienced member leading each pair, and I give each pair a section of the schematic so the work does not overlap. I make sure the right tools are there, including crimpers and a torque screwdriver. I check the first few terminations of each person and correct any problems straight away. Each pair ticks off each wire on a check print as they finish it, and any difference from the drawing is reported to me, not changed on the spot. I approve changes and mark them up. At the end of each day I compare progress with the plan. When a panel is finished, a member of the other pair does the point-to-point check, and I sign it off.
markingPoints: Controls drawings so everyone uses the latest set
Sets and shows the standard; supplies correct tools
Organises pairs and sections; checks early work
Uses check prints and controlled mark-ups for changes
Tracks progress and uses an independent check before sign-off

essays.stem: Explain how the site environment in Jamaica (salt air, heat, dust, humidity and storms) affects the choice and mounting of panels and equipment.
essays.modelAnswer: Near the coast, salt air corrodes mild steel and copper quickly, so I would choose stainless steel or suitable plastic enclosures, stainless fixings and sealed glands, and keep the doors closed with good gaskets. High temperatures reduce the life of drives, UPS units and electronics, so panels need ventilation, filtered fans or air-conditioning as the maker says, and should be kept out of direct sun or given a sun shield. Dust from roads, quarries or factories can block filters and cause tracking, so I choose the right IP rating and arrange for filters to be cleaned. Humidity can cause condensation inside enclosures, which damages parts and causes faults, so anti-condensation heaters or breathers may be needed, and cable entries are sealed. Heavy rain and storms mean outdoor equipment must be mounted above possible flood level, firmly anchored against hurricane winds, and fitted with surge protection against lightning. The specification sets these needs, and I check each one when equipment is mounted.
markingPoints: Salt air: corrosion-resistant enclosures, fixings and glands
Heat: ventilation or cooling, shade from direct sun
Dust: IP rating and filter maintenance
Humidity: condensation control and sealed entries
Storms and floods: mounting height, anchoring and surge protection

essays.stem: Explain the documents produced during the installation and commissioning of equipment, and why each one matters to the client.
essays.modelAnswer: The receiving records show what was delivered and in what condition, which supports any claim against the supplier. The inspection and test plan lists every check, who does it and who signs, so nothing is missed. Marked-up drawings record every change made during installation, and become the as-built drawings, so future electricians can trace wiring and find faults. Test results, such as continuity and insulation readings, prove the work was safe before it was energised and give a baseline for later tests. Commissioning sheets record settings, such as overload and timer settings, the function tests and who witnessed them, so the client can see that the equipment works as designed and can restore the settings if a part is replaced. The punch list shows defects and when they were cleared. The makers' manuals and warranties explain operation and maintenance and protect the client if something fails. Together they let the client accept the work, run it safely and maintain it.
markingPoints: Receiving records and inspection and test plan
Marked-up and as-built drawings
Test results as proof and baseline
Commissioning sheets with settings and witnesses; punch list
Manuals and warranties; overall value to the client

essays.stem: A pump station panel uses a PLC with float switches, a pressure switch and a 4–20 mA pressure transmitter. Explain how you would check the field wiring while it is isolated, and what the competent person checks when it is energised.
essays.modelAnswer: With the panel isolated, locked off, tagged and proved dead with a tester checked before and after, I take the I/O list and the drawings. I check each field cable is the right type, correctly glanded, labelled and landed on the right terminals. I check continuity of each input loop from the terminal to the device and back, operating each float switch and the pressure switch by hand to see the contact open and close on the meter. For the transmitter, I check its polarity and that the screen is earthed at one end only, as the design says. I check insulation of the field cables with the PLC and transmitter disconnected, so the test voltage cannot damage them. I record each result against the I/O list. When the competent person energises the panel, they check that each input shows correctly on the PLC as each device is operated, that the transmitter reads about 4 mA at zero pressure and changes as pressure rises, and that the pump starts, stops and alarms at the right levels.
markingPoints: Safe isolation and use of the I/O list and drawings
Checks cable type, glands, labels and terminations
Continuity checks while operating each switch; transmitter polarity and screen
Insulation test with electronics disconnected; results recorded
Energised checks by a competent person: inputs, 4 mA zero, pump control and alarms

practical1.title: Mount and secondary-wire a control panel from drawings
practical1.brief: The assessor gives the group a panel layout drawing, a schematic and a terminal diagram for a small motor control panel: incoming isolator and MCB, a 24 V control transformer or supply, a contactor, an overload relay, a time-delay relay, terminal blocks, and START, STOP and indicator lamps on the door. The panel is NOT connected to any supply. As a group, plan the work and give each member a section: mounting DIN rail and duct, mounting the parts, door wiring, power wiring and control wiring. Mount the parts to the layout drawing. Wire to the schematic, with a number marker at both ends of each wire, ferrules on stranded wire, terminals tightened to the maker's torque, field connections on terminal blocks, and a flexible earth strap to the door. Mark any change on the drawing. When the panel is finished, a different member checks each section point to point against the drawings with a continuity tester, ticking each wire. Then carry out protective conductor continuity and insulation tests on the power circuit, and record all results. The assessor then energises the control circuit, with the motor supply isolated, and the group watches the function test.
materials: Panel enclosure with back plate, DIN rail and slotted wiring duct
Isolator, MCB, control transformer or 24 V supply, contactor, overload relay, time-delay relay and terminal blocks
Push-buttons and indicator lamps for the door; flexible earth strap
Control wire, wire markers, ferrules and a ferrule crimper
Torque screwdriver, hand tools and a drill for the back plate
Panel layout drawing, schematic, terminal diagram and test record sheet (from the assessor)
photos: The group's work plan with sections given out
The back plate with rail, duct and parts mounted
Close-up of wire markers and ferrules at a terminal
The finished panel with duct covers off
The check print with each wire ticked during the point-to-point check
The control circuit function test by the assessor
checklist: Mounted their parts to the layout drawing, level and secure
Wired their section correctly to the schematic
Marked each wire at both ends to match the drawing
Fitted ferrules and tightened terminals to the torque figure
Checked another member's section point to point and recorded findings
Carried out a continuity or insulation test correctly
Recorded changes on the drawing and kept the area tidy
safety: The panel is never connected to a supply while the group works on it; only the assessor energises it
Wear safety glasses when drilling and cutting duct and rail
Deburr cut rail and duct so nobody is cut
Warn others before each insulation test
Stay back from the panel while the assessor carries out the function test

practical2.title: Receive, mount and connect a pump-station control panel with its field devices
practical2.brief: The assessor sets up a pump-station training mock-up: a wall-mounted control panel (about 30 to 40 kg) delivered in its packing, a delivery note and order, a training wall, a tank mock-up with two float switches, a pressure switch, and a pressure transmitter, with an I/O list and drawings. Nothing is connected to any supply. As a group, carry out the receiving inspection: check the panel against the order and the nameplate, note any damage, and record it. Plan how to lift and mount the panel safely using a lifting aid or a team lift, and record the plan. Mark out and fix strut channel to the wall with suitable anchors, then hang the panel level with the clear space required in front. Run and gland the field cables to each device, keeping the transmitter's signal cable away from power cables, and land them on the terminal blocks to the drawings. Each member installs and connects at least one device. With the panel isolated and locked off, check each input loop with a continuity tester while operating the device by hand, and record the results on the I/O list. Fit blanking plugs and labels. Finally the assessor energises the panel and the group records the function test on a commissioning sheet.
materials: Wall-mounted control panel in its packing, with delivery note, order and nameplate data
Training wall, strut channel, anchors, fixings and a lifting aid or panel lifter
Two float switches, a pressure switch and a pressure transmitter on a tank mock-up
Field cable, screened signal cable, cable glands, blanking plugs and labels
SDS drill with dust extraction, spirit level, laser level, cable detector and hand tools
Continuity and insulation tester; lock-off kit and padlocks
I/O list, drawings, receiving form, lift plan sheet and commissioning sheet
photos: The completed receiving form with the nameplate in view
The written lift plan and the panel being lifted safely
The panel mounted level on strut channel
